bites.title: A brush is a recipe
bites.body: A Krita brush preset is a recipe: a tip (the shape of each dab), plus settings that react to your pen. Three dials on the top toolbar change any brush on the fly: Size, Opacity, Flow.

bites.title: Try a different brush
bites.body: Open Brush Presets ({key:show_brush_presets|F6}) and pick anything that looks fun. Pencils, inks, a bristle brush. Scribble with it.

bites.title: Size
bites.body: Drag the Size slider on the top toolbar. Make it at least half again bigger or smaller.

bites.title: Opacity: the darkest a stroke can get
bites.body: Drag Opacity below 50%. Now paint a stroke, lift, and paint over it. See it build up where the strokes cross? Opacity caps each stroke, not the painting.

bites.title: Flow: how much paint per dab
bites.body: Now drag Flow below 50% and paint one long stroke that crosses back over itself. Flow builds up within a single stroke, like an airbrush. Opacity builds up between strokes.

bites.title: Back to full strength
bites.body: Put Opacity back near 100% (press O a few times, or drag it).

bites.title: Under the hood
bites.body: Press {key:show_brush_editor|F5}: the Brush Editor. Every setting the pen can drive lives here: size, opacity, rotation. Peek, then close it. Lesson 18 is all about this.

bites.title: Every brush is an eraser
bites.body: Press {key:erase_action|E}. Your current brush now erases. Same shape, same pressure. Press E again to go back.

bites.title: 03 cleared
bites.body: Preset, size, opacity, flow, the editor, eraser mode. You can read any brush now.
